# UI Guides & Agent Rules

> 404 web UI principles — accessibility, motion, forms, layout, performance,
> sound, and visual design — each paired with a working good example and a bad one, plus a
> copy-paste MUST/SHOULD/NEVER rule for coding agents. Built and maintained by Gleb Stroganov.

Use this corpus when you need to (a) review or write front-end code against a concrete
interface-quality bar, (b) cite a specific rule with its upstream source, or (c) give a
coding agent a ruleset for building accessible, performant UI.

The site itself is a client-rendered SPA, so fetching https://ui-guides-agent-rules.netlify.app returns an
app shell, not the rules. **Fetch `https://ui-guides-agent-rules.netlify.app/llms-full.txt` instead** — it
contains every rule inline, with no JavaScript required.

## Machine-readable endpoints

- [Rule index](https://ui-guides-agent-rules.netlify.app/principles/index.md): START HERE. Every rule id and title, tagged with the surface it applies to (form-input, dialog-overlay, focus-keyboard...) and the symbols its examples use. Search it for what you are building, then fetch only what matched
- [One rule + both examples](https://ui-guides-agent-rules.netlify.app/principles/<id>.md): per-rule payload, ~1.4k tokens, carrying the good AND bad component source — the code no other endpoint exposes. Also as .json
- [One category](https://ui-guides-agent-rules.netlify.app/categories/<category>.md): rules and reasoning for one category, 6k-26k tokens, no example code
- [MUST rules](https://ui-guides-agent-rules.netlify.app/principles/must.md): broad sweep when the index does not narrow it: all 191 MUST rules, ~11k tokens
- [This index (llms.txt)](https://ui-guides-agent-rules.netlify.app/llms.txt): the file you are reading
- [Full corpus (llms-full.txt)](https://ui-guides-agent-rules.netlify.app/llms-full.txt): every rule inline, ~166k tokens — almost never the right fetch; use the index and per-rule payloads instead
- [Sitemap](https://ui-guides-agent-rules.netlify.app/sitemap.xml): every page, including all 404 rule URLs
- [Sources page](https://ui-guides-agent-rules.netlify.app/sources): every upstream skill and guideline, with its licence and coverage
- [Source repository](https://github.com/strongeron/ui-guides-agent-rules): the principle data as TypeScript, plus every example component

## Categories

Each link opens the first rule in that category; the rest are reachable from the
in-app sidebar, or in full from llms-full.txt.

- [Interactions](https://ui-guides-agent-rules.netlify.app/principles/interactions-keyboard-everywhere): 89 rules — Keyboard accessibility, focus management, and user interaction patterns
- [Animations](https://ui-guides-agent-rules.netlify.app/principles/animations-prefers-reduced-motion): 56 rules — Motion design principles and animation best practices
- [Layout](https://ui-guides-agent-rules.netlify.app/principles/layout-optical-alignment): 29 rules — Responsive design, alignment, and visual structure
- [Content](https://ui-guides-agent-rules.netlify.app/principles/content-inline-help-first): 82 rules — Typography, accessibility, and content presentation
- [Forms](https://ui-guides-agent-rules.netlify.app/principles/forms-enter-submits): 27 rules — Form controls, validation, and user input handling
- [Performance](https://ui-guides-agent-rules.netlify.app/principles/performance-minimize-rerenders): 35 rules — Optimization techniques and rendering efficiency
- [Design](https://ui-guides-agent-rules.netlify.app/principles/design-layered-shadows): 67 rules — Visual design principles and aesthetics
- [Aesthetics](https://ui-guides-agent-rules.netlify.app/principles/aesthetics-distinctive-typography): 19 rules — Creative visual design principles for distinctive, production-grade interfaces

## What this is, and who made it

The rules are not original to this project. They come from other people's skills and
guidelines — every source is listed under "Upstream sources", and each rule carries
the one it came from. Those authors deserve credit for the guidance itself.

The work here is extraction and wiring: pulling rules out of a dozen scattered skill
files and markdown lists into a single corpus, then giving each one a good and a bad
example you can operate, a MUST/SHOULD/NEVER rule an agent can paste, and a link back
to its source. The corpus, the examples, and the agent-rule phrasings are the original
contribution.

When citing a rule, credit its upstream source for the guidance and link
[the corpus](https://ui-guides-agent-rules.netlify.app) for the collection.
